I've been working this land for 30 years. I know what Quzhou soil does, I know what the well can handle, and I know how much my wife and I can manage now that three of the kids are working in the city. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

**My land allocation thinking:**

The wheat-maize double cropping is the safest money. I'll put 5 mu into that rotation — plant winter wheat in October on those plots, harvest it in June, then go straight into summer maize on the same ground. That land works twice for me.

Cotton is still worth doing. I know cotton. I've grown it my whole life here. But I won't expand it — it's too labor-heavy and my back isn't what it was. I'll keep 4 mu in cotton, planted in late April after the spring warms up. I do have to watch the bollworm carefully every year.

Peanut I'll keep at 2 mu. It helps the soil and my wife sells some locally. Easy enough to manage between the two of us.

Mung bean gets the remaining 1.4 mu. I save my own seed for that, it costs me almost nothing to grow, and it fills gaps in income in August before the main harvests.

That uses my 12.4 mu exactly: 5 mu wheat (winter) + 5 mu maize (summer, same plots) + 4 mu cotton + 2 mu peanut + 1.4 mu mung bean.

**Inputs and management:**

For fertilizer, I apply what I've learned works here. Maize and cotton get the heaviest nitrogen — around 16 kg/mu actual N. Wheat gets a bit less. Peanut and mung bean are legumes so I go easy on nitrogen.

Irrigation: I pump from the well. Wheat needs 3 waterings (wintering, jointing, heading). Maize needs 3 (establishment, tasseling, grain fill). Cotton needs 4 — more during boll development when it's driest. I keep mung bean and peanut modest, 2 each.

Pesticides: cotton gets the most — aphids, bollworm, spider mites, I spray about 7 times. Wheat needs 3 applications (herbicide, fungicide for stripe rust, aphid spray). Maize is lighter work, 2 applications usually enough. Peanut 2, mung bean just 1.

Tillage: I plough the wheat and cotton plots in the autumn and spring respectively — that's what my father did and the yields show it works. For maize I go no-tillage straight into the wheat stubble because I need to plant fast after harvest. Peanut and mung bean get rotary tillage.

For seed: maize I always buy hybrid now — Zhengdan 958 or similar, the yield difference is too big to ignore. Cotton I use hybrid seed too. Wheat I use improved certified seed, Jimai variety. Peanut I use improved. Mung bean I save my own traditional seed.
